aria: Animated recap of the Kings' 97 to 96 home win over the Celtics: Keegan Murray's putback tip-in with 5 seconds left that turned a one-point deficit into the win, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Darius Acuff Jr.'s 21 points and 8 assists, the top scorers, how Sacramento won, and Monday's game against the Spurs.

notes: Box score from the Kings' 97–96 home win over the Boston Celtics on Nov 21, 2026, from the boxscore.email box score, checked against the Associated Press, Field Level Media (95.3 The Score), Ball Exclusives (Yardbarker), Sports Radio Service and Celtics On SI. The player lines add up to both team totals (97 and 96). The quarter scores (25–16–35–21 to 27–27–13–29) add up to both totals: Boston led 54–41 at the half and Sacramento led 76–67 after three (AP; Sports Radio Service). Boston's biggest lead was 13, at the half (Celtics On SI; Ball Exclusives); no source gives Sacramento's biggest lead, so it is left out. Free throws (26 of 32 to 15 of 25), field goals (32 of 78 to 34 of 101), threes (7 of 26 to 13 of 58), blocks, assists and steals are from the box score; Celtics On SI also has Boston's 13 of 58 from three (a franchise record 45 misses). Celtics On SI says Boston forced 20 turnovers; the box score lists 18, so turnovers are left out. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Saturday's games.

Sacramento snapped an eight-game losing streak and won at home for the first time this season (AP); Ball Exclusives has the Kings 1–9 at home. Boston was without Jayson Tatum (rest), Derrick White (shoulder) and Mitchell Robinson (illness) (AP). The Kings won the third quarter 35–13 while Boston missed all 13 of its threes in the quarter (AP). Darius Acuff Jr. scored 9 of his 21 in the fourth quarter (Sports Radio Service). Payton Pritchard put Boston up 96–95 with 11.8 seconds left; Acuff drove the lane and missed, and Keegan Murray put it back with 5.0 seconds left; Pritchard's 20-footer at the buzzer missed (AP; Field Level Media; Ball Exclusives: "The go-ahead basket came with 5.0 left"). The Kings host San Antonio on Monday, Nov 23 at 10:00 PM ET (Ball Exclusives; AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Keegan Murray's putback with 5.0 seconds left that made it 97–96 (AP: "Murray grabbed the putback and scored to give the Kings the one-point advantage"; Celtics On SI (Kings): "a putback tip-in"; ClutchPoints: "Murray crashed the glass and put it back in"). The template draws it as a finish at the rim; Acuff's missed drive and the rebound are not animated, and no source says which side of the rim it came from. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Sacramento Kings or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The player in the play of the game is drawn to Keegan Murray's listed 6-foot-8 and 225 pounds with No. 13 (Basketball-Reference; Tankathon), with his arms scaled to a reported 6-foot-11 wingspan (The Kings Herald). He is drawn in Sacramento's home white with the default figure look (no approved look yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
